One: He will forgive you your disbelief and your fighting against the Messenger of Allah; this was said by al-Zajjaj.

The second: He will forgive you your going out with the polytheists; this was said by Ibn Zayd in the completion of his first statement.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 8, verse 71:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if they intend your betrayal﴾ means: if the captives intend to betray you by disbelief after Islam. ﴿Then they had betrayed Allah before﴾ when they disbelieved in Him before their capture. Ibn Zayd said: "Then they had betrayed by their going out with the polytheists." We have already mentioned from him that it was revealed concerning a people who professed Islam verbally. Muqatil said: the meaning is, if they betray you, I will enable you over them, so you will kill them and take them captive, as I enabled you at Badr. Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of any betrayal if they commit it, ﴿Wise﴾ in His management concerning them and in His recompense to them.

Ibn al-Jawzi, Zad al-Masir, on Surah 8, verse 72:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ means the emigrants (muhajirun), who abandoned their homes, their wealth, and their people in support of the religion (p-385). ﴿And those who gave shelter and helped﴾ means the Helpers (ansar), who sheltered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), settled the emigrants in their homes, and helped them against their enemies. ﴿Those are allies of one another.﴾ Regarding "allies of one another" there are two views:

One: in support. The second: in inheritance.

The exegetes said: They used to inherit from one another by virtue of emigration, and a believer who had not emigrated did not inherit from his emigrant relative. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿You have no obligation of guardianship toward them until they emigrate﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and al-Kisa'i read "wilayatihim" with a fatha on the waw. Hamzah read it with a kasra on the waw. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: there is no inheritance between you and them until they emigrate. Whoever reads the waw of wilaya with a kasra, it is equivalent to leadership (imarah); and when it is read with a fatha, it is from support. Yunus al-Nahwi said: "al-wilaya" with a fatha belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while "al-wilaya" with a kasra comes from "walitu al-amr" (I held the affair). Abu 'Ubayda said: "al-wilaya" with a fatha is for the Creator, and "al-wilaya" with a kasra is for the created. Ibn al-Anbari said: "al-wilaya" with a fatha is the verbal noun of "al-wali" (the protector), and "al-wilaya" with a kasra is the verbal noun of "al-wali" (the ruler); it is said "waliyyun bayna al-wilaya" and "wali bayna al-wilaya." This is the preferred view, though it may also apply in other cases. Ibn Faris said: "al-wilaya" with a fatha means support, and it may be read with a kasra; "al-wilaya" with a kasra means authority (sultan).

Section

Some people held that the intended meaning of this guardianship is allegiance of support and affection. They said: this ruling was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [At-Tawbah: 71]. As for those who said it refers to inheritance, they said: it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿But blood relatives are more entitled to one another﴾ [Al-Anfal: 75].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they seek your help in religion﴾ means: if the believers who have not emigrated seek your help, then help them, except against a people between whom and you there is a covenant, for then do not betray those bound by the covenant. Some said: it was not obligatory for the emigrant to help one who had not emigrated unless he sought his help.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 8, verse 73–74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾, concerning this there are two views.

One: it concerns inheritance. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it concerns support (nusrah). This is the view of Qatadah.

Concerning His saying: ﴿unless you do it﴾, there are two views.

One: it refers to inheritance, so the meaning is: unless you act upon inheritance as I have commanded you. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it refers to mutual support, so the meaning is: unless you cooperate and support one another in the religion. This is the view of Ibn Jurayj. Its explanation: when a believer does not take a believer as a true ally (tawalli haqqan) and does not thoroughly disassociate (tabarri) from the disbeliever, this leads to misguidance and corruption in the religion. So when a Muslim forsakes his disbelieving relatives and supports the Muslims, this is more likely to draw his disbelieving relatives toward Islam and to abandon shirk.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and great corruption﴾. Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Sirin and Ibn al-Sumayfa' read it as "kathir" with the letter tha' (ث).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾, that is: they are those who have actualised their faith through what it requires of emigration (hijrah) and support, unlike one who remains in the abode of shirk. And "generous provision" (al-rizq al-karim) is that which is good, and that is in Paradise.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 8, verse 75:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who believed after [that]﴾ — that is, after the first emigrants (al-muhajirun al-awwalun). Ibn Abbas said: They are those who emigrated after al-Hudaybiyya.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another﴾ — that is, in inheritance by virtue of emigration. Ibn Abbas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established brotherhood between his companions, and they would inherit from one another by that brotherhood, until this verse was revealed, and they then inherited by lineage."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ — concerning this there are three opinions.

The first: that it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

The second: that it is the Qur'an, which had explained to them the division of inheritance in the surah of al-Nisa' (4:11-12).

The third: that it is the judgment of Allah, mentioned by al-Zajjaj.
